topics.title: Getting started
topics.description: Fast orientation to chat, sidebars, and key actions.

topics.title: Grand tour
topics.description: A guided walkthrough of every major area — chat, galleries, creative tools, contacts, import, and configuration.

steps.text: Welcome to the grand tour. Use the Guide button any time to reopen this list or pick a focused topic for deeper help.
The chat box is home base. Ask natural-language questions about your archive — emails, messages, photos, contacts, and more.
Open Personality Settings from the portrait in the top bar. Choose your AI provider, voice persona, creativity, and who is asking (owner or visitor).
The context bar above the chat shows how many AI tools and reference documents are active, plus token use from your last request.
Click Tools in the context bar to review which archive tools the AI may call (Configuration → Tools Access).
Click Ref Docs to open the Reference Documents manager — upload PDFs, Markdown, or text the AI can use in answers.
Click the tool-call count to inspect which archive searches ran on your last chat request.
Messages — browse SMS, WhatsApp, iMessage, and other imported conversations by contact.
Emails — search and read your imported Gmail and IMAP mail in a gallery with filters and sort.
Images — search photos by metadata, tags, date, region, or semantic content similarity.
Facebook Albums — browse imported Facebook photo albums.
Facebook Posts — read imported Facebook posts and their text.
Multi-Source Search — find related content across emails, messages, and posts by concept, not just keywords.
Locations — explore places mentioned or geotagged in your archive.
Artefacts — curate named collections with descriptions, stories, and attached files or gallery images.
Previous Responses — revisit and resume saved chat turns.
Suggestions — ready-made prompts to explore your archive; click one to fill the chat input.
Contacts and Relationships — directory of people, email matching, classifications, and the relationship graph.
Open the Relationships tab to visualise who connects to whom and how strongly, based on message traffic.
Profiles — AI-generated biographical profiles for contacts, editable and regeneratable.
Sensitive Data — encrypted notes unlocked with your master key; separate from the main archive tables.
Dashboard — record counts and a snapshot of what is in your archive.
Have-a-Chat — watch two AI personas discuss a topic using your archive as context.
Random Question — generate a surprising question about the archive to spark exploration.
Today's Thing — a daily prompt drawn from the subject's interests in Configuration.
Interviewer — structured AI-led interviews using archive data, with saved sessions.
Identity Profile — a guided wizard to capture life story, health, family, career, and interests for the subject.
Import & Manage Data — upload Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, iMessage, Gmail, photos, and run maintenance jobs.
The Maintenance and Background Jobs tabs schedule thumbnails, embeddings, and other housekeeping tasks.
Configuration — appearance, API keys, subject details, regions, suggestions, guide topics, custom voices, visitor keys, and tool access.
API Keys — connect Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek. Local AI (Ollama) needs no cloud key.
Subject Configuration — name, pronouns, interests, writing style, and psychological profile for the archive owner.
Custom Voices — create persona instructions the AI can adopt in chat and creative tools.
Manage Visitor Keys — issue keys so guests can unlock shared views without the owner's master password.
Tools Access — choose which AI archive tools require owner vs visitor tier for each session.
That completes the grand tour. Reopen Guide anytime and pick a focused topic — Browsing emails, Import paths, Master key setup, and others — for step-by-step detail on any area.

topics.title: Quick setup checklist
topics.description: A short first-run flow: import, configure, ask a question, unlock.

topics.title: Archive selection at sign-in
topics.description: Choose the right user archive before entering password.

steps.text: On the login screen, the selected user determines which archive database is active.
If multiple users exist, confirm the selected name before signing in.
If sign-in fails unexpectedly, switch away and back to the target user once, then try again.

topics.title: Asking questions
topics.description: Get better answers and steer perspective and tone.

steps.text: Type your question in chat and press Send. Try: "Tell me about Dave's friends" or "Show me photos from last summer" or "Who have I emailed most?"
Use AI Personality settings to change the response style and mood.
When the Personality Settings dialog is open you can set characteristice of the conversation or clear the the conversation history and start a new conversation.
Switch "Who's Asking?" to frame answers from visitor or owner perspective.

topics.title: Browsing emails
topics.description: Search, filter, sort, and read your imported email archive.

steps.text: Open Emails in the left sidebar to browse your imported email collection.
Type a keyword, sender name, or subject in the Search box and press the search button to filter results.
Use the Year filter to narrow down emails to a particular year.
Change the Sort order (newest first, oldest first) to control how results are listed.
Click any email in the list to open and read its full content, including attachments.
You can also ask the AI directly: "Summarise emails from Alice in March" or "Find emails about the conference booking".

topics.title: Browsing images
topics.description: Find memories in photo galleries, albums, and posts.

steps.text: Open Images in the left sidebar to browse your photo collection. Images from multiple sources are combined into a single gallery.
Use the Search box to find photos by caption, description, or tag.

Similar images are found by comparing the visual content of the images using AI embedding search. Searches are based on the image tags which can be either added to the image manually or extracted from the image using the AI to classify the content.
Click on any image to open the image and see it in fullsize
Ctrl+Click on any image to select it and then apply one of the Bulk Actions to it. Ctrl+Shift+Click on any image to select a range of images.
Open Facebook Albums to browse imported album collections.
Open Facebook Posts to browse imported posts that may contain photos.
Ask the AI: "Find photos with John" or "Show me photos from last Christmas".

topics.title: Browsing messages
topics.description: Navigate your imported SMS, WhatsApp, Facebook, and iMessage conversations.

steps.text: Open Messages in the left sidebar to browse your imported SMS and chat conversations. This covers WhatsApp, iMessage, Facebook Messenger, Instagram and SMS messages imported into your archive.
Conversations are grouped by contact. Indivdual contacts are shown first and Group contacts are shown last. Scroll through the list or search by name to find a specific person.
Click any conversation to open the full message thread. Each message shows its timestamp and direction (sent/received).
Ask the AI about your messages: "What did Bob last say to me?" or "Show conversations about the holiday from 2023".

topics.title: Exploring locations
topics.description: Browse geographic locations extracted from your photos and archive data.

steps.text: Open Locations in the left sidebar to browse places from your archive — GPS coordinates from photos, location tags, and check-ins.
Locations are grouped by category and region. Browse by area to revisit places you have been.
Click a location to see related photos or archive items from that place.
Use the layers button to toggle the display of the different location categories on the map.
The map will only display a limited number of photos at a time. Click the Shuffle button to see more photos.
To filter the photos by region, select a region from the Region dropdown menu.
Ask the AI for location-based summaries: "Where have I travelled most?" or "Show me photos from Paris".

topics.title: Artefacts — notes and custom items
topics.description: Create, search, import, and export personal artefact records in your archive.

steps.text: Open Artefacts from the left sidebar. Artefacts are personal notes, items, and custom records you attach to your archive — think of them as a display case of meaningful items.
Click "+ New Artefact" to create a new record. Each artefact can have a name, description, tags, images, and a story section.
Use the Search box to find artefacts by name, description, tags, or story text.
Use Export to download all artefacts as a JSON file, or Import to load artefacts from a previously exported file.
Artefacts are searchable by the AI: ask "Tell me about my artefact about the vintage watch" or "List artefacts tagged family".

topics.title: Managing Contacts
topics.description: Use Contacts and Relationships, Profiles, and contact tools effectively.

steps.text: Open Contacts and Relationships in the right sidebar to browse people or open the Relationships tab for the connection map.
The Contacts and Relationships dialog is used to manage the contacts and relationships in your archive. It is used to create, edit, and delete contacts and relationships.
Open Profiles to view detailed notes and relationship context.
Use the Relationships tab for a visual network of people and connection strength.
Use Configuration to classify contacts and tune contact recognition.

topics.title: Relationship map
topics.description: Visualise your social network and connection strengths.

steps.text: Open Contacts and Relationships in the right sidebar to access the relationship tools.
The relationship map is shown on the Relationships tab inside the Contacts dialog. This shows a visual network map of people connected to you.
Node size and link thickness reflect connection strength — people you communicate with most appear more prominently.
Click any node in the network to highlight that person and their direct connections.
Ask the AI about your relationships: "Who am I closest to based on my messages?" or "Who connects me to the Smith family?"

topics.title: Create a profile for a contact
topics.description: Generate, review, and edit AI-written complete profiles for people in your archive.

steps.text: A complete profile is an AI-written summary of one contact drawn from their messages, emails, and other archive material. It helps you (and the chat AI) understand who someone is, how they relate to you, and how they communicate.
The contact must already exist in your archive—usually from an import (Gmail, WhatsApp, Facebook, and so on). More messages and emails generally produce a richer profile.
Open Profiles from the right sidebar. This is the main place to create and manage complete profiles.
Choose the AI provider used to write the profile. Gemini, Claude, and DeepSeek need a configured API key under Configuration → API Keys; Local AI needs Ollama running with a chat model installed.

Click the Contact field and type part of a name to filter the list. Tick one or more checkboxes to select who should get a new profile. You can select several people and create profiles for all of them in one go.
When at least one contact is selected, click Create profile. Generation runs in the background and may take several minutes per person—you can keep using the app while it works.
Watch the Contacts with complete profiles table below. While a profile is being written, the name shows (generating…). The list refreshes automatically every few seconds while this dialog stays open.
When generation finishes, click a contact name in that table to open their profile, or use Actions → View profile on their row.
The profile opens in a View tab with rendered Markdown—sections about the person, your relationship, communication style, and themes from their archive data.
To adjust the text yourself, switch to the Edit tab. You can fix facts, add private context, or trim sections the AI overstated. Profiles still generating cannot be edited yet.
Click Save to store your edits. Switch back to View to see the rendered Markdown after saving.
To replace an existing profile with a fresh AI pass, open Actions on that row in Profiles and choose Regenerate…. The old text is overwritten when the new generation completes.
Shortcut from the contact directory: open Contacts and Relationships, find someone, and click the sync icon on their row to start profile generation using your current chat AI provider.
In Contacts, use Search to filter by name or email when the directory is long. Only contacts with imported conversation history can produce a meaningful profile.
You can ask the chat AI about someone once a profile exists—for example: "Summarise my relationship with [name]" or "How does [name] usually communicate with me?"

topics.title: Switching AI provider
topics.description: Choose between Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Local AI at any time.

steps.text: The AI provider can be switched at any time without restarting. Open the voice and AI settings panel from the top bar.
The Provider dropdown lists all configured providers: Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), DeepSeek, and Local AI (Ollama). Select a different one to switch immediately.
Cloud providers (Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek) require an API key set in Configuration → API Keys. If a provider is greyed out or unavailable, check that its key is entered.
Local AI (Ollama/Gemma4) requires Ollama to be running and the required models downloaded. Use Configuration → Local AI Setup to check status.
Each provider has different strengths: Claude and Gemini excel at reasoning and long context; DeepSeek is cost-effective; Local AI is fully private with no internet required.

topics.title: Understanding the context bar
topics.description: Use the chat context bar to manage AI tools and reference documents.

steps.text: The context status bar sits just below the chat input and shows the number of AI tool available, the  number of reference documents available to the AI and the AI usage statistics of you most rescent request.
The Tools segment shows how many AI tools are currently active for this session. Click it to open the Tools Access configuration.
The Ref Docs segment shows how many reference documents are available. Click it to open the Reference Documents manager.
The tools call log segment shows the number of tool calls made in the most recent chat request. Click it to open the tool call log.
A warning icon on either segment means something may need attention — for example, no tools are enabled or no documents are loaded. Click the segment to resolve it.

topics.title: Previous responses
topics.description: Browse and revisit your previously saved AI chat responses.

steps.text: Open Previous Responses in the right sidebar to browse AI answers you have saved from past chat sessions.
Responses are listed in reverse chronological order. Each entry shows the question asked and a preview of the AI's answer.
Click any saved response to expand it and read the full content, including any images or formatted sections.
To save a new response, use the save (bookmark) icon that appears on an AI chat bubble after the response completes.

topics.title: Using suggestions
topics.description: Discover pre-written prompts organised by topic to jumpstart conversations.

steps.text: Open Suggestions from the right sidebar to browse a library of ready-made prompts grouped by topic.
Suggestions are grouped into categories such as Messages, Emails, Photos, and Relationships. Scroll or expand a category to see individual prompts.
Click any suggestion to send it directly to the chat input. The suggestion text is pre-filled — you can edit it before sending or send it as-is.
Administrators can customise the suggestion library via Configuration → Suggestions — adding, editing, and removing prompts, or importing a new set.

topics.title: Today's Thing of Interest
topics.description: Generate fresh prompts based on interests.

steps.text: Today's Thing of Interest suggests memory prompts or news from the web based on subject interests.
Click repeatedly for different suggestions.
Add more interests in Configuration → Subject Configuration for better variety.

topics.title: Email catchup
topics.description: Get back up to speed on imported mail and use AI to summarise threads, senders, and topics.

steps.text: Open Emails from the left sidebar. Your imported Gmail and IMAP messages live here — use this gallery to skim before you ask the AI for summaries.
Narrow to the period you want to catch up on. Set the Year and Month filters, then click Search. For a broad recent sweep, pick the current year and leave month as All.
Sort newest first so the most recent mail appears at the top of the list.
Optionally filter by sender in the From box if you already know who you need to catch up with.
Click any message in the list to read it in the detail pane — useful for quickly checking something before you ask for an AI summary.
With an email open, use Ask the AI for a focused question about that message only (tone, action items, who else was copied, and so on).
Close the email gallery when you are ready to summarise across many messages at once.
Ask the chat for a recent overview. Try: "Summarise my emails from this week" or "What did I miss in my inbox last month?"
Drill into one person: "Summarise emails from Alice since January" or "What has Mum emailed about lately?"
Drill into a topic or project: "Find emails about the house move and summarise the timeline" or "What open threads do I have about the conference?"
Tip: the Suggestions sidebar includes ready-made email prompts if you want inspiration for your next question.

topics.title: Multi-Source Similarity search
topics.description: Find semantically related messages, emails, photos, and posts using AI embedding search.

steps.text: Open Multi-Source Search from the left sidebar. This uses AI embeddings to find content that is conceptually similar to your query — not just keyword matches.
Type a concept, phrase, or sentence in the search box. For example: "arguments about money" or "planning a holiday" or "feeling sad about dad".
Set the number of results (default 25). More results give broader coverage but may include less relevant items.
Click Search to run the query. Results are returned across all source types — messages, emails, Facebook posts, and albums — and grouped by tab.
Switch between the result tabs (Messages, Emails, Posts, Albums) to see which sources had the most relevant matches.
Similarity search requires embeddings to be generated for your archive data. If results are sparse, run the embedding background jobs in Import & Manage Data → Background Jobs.

topics.title: Have-a-Chat — two AI voices
topics.description: Watch two AI personas have a conversation about your archive.

steps.text: Open Have-a-Chat from the right sidebar. This feature runs a conversation between two AI voices about your archive data — like listening to two people talk about you.

Enter a topic or question to guide the conversation. For example: "Discuss the most important relationships in the archive" or "What do the messages reveal about work stress?" Leave blank to let the AIs explore freely.
Choose the voice and AI provider for each participant (Voice A and Voice B). Each can use a different provider and persona.
Optionally enable Banter Mode for a more playful exchange, or adjust Temperature to control how creative the conversation becomes.
Set Free-Run Rounds to let the conversation continue automatically for a set number of exchanges before pausing for your review.
Click Start Chat to begin. The conversation appears in the main chat area. You can Pause at any point or Inject a comment to steer the discussion.
While running, use Inject Comment to add your own message into the conversation, or Stop to end the session. You will be asked whether to save the conversation.
Review previous conversations via the Previous Conversations button. Saved sessions can be downloaded as Markdown.

topics.title: Interviewer
topics.description: Conduct a structured AI-driven Q&A session and save the results.

steps.text: Open Interviewer from the right sidebar. The Interviewer runs a structured question-and-answer session where the AI asks questions and you (or the archive subject) answer them.
Choose an interview topic or theme. The AI will ask a series of questions based on your archive data, tailored to the subject's history and relationships.
Answer each question in the input box and press Send. The AI reads your answer and asks a follow-up question, building a narrative conversation.

When the interview is complete, the AI creates a summary of the interview and it is saved to your archive. You can review past interviews at any time from the Interviewer panel which will display a list of past interviews if available.

topics.title: Random question
topics.description: Get a spontaneous question about your archive to spark a conversation.

steps.text: Open Random Question from the right sidebar. This feature generates a random, archive-aware question to start a conversation — useful when you do not know what to ask.
A question is generated based on your archive contents and subject configuration. Click it to send it to the chat, or click Generate Another to get a different question.
Questions are drawn from your actual data — contacts, events, photos, and message themes — so each one is unique to your archive.
When the AI has generated a question (and the AI is behaving itself), you can click the Anser button to get he AI to answer the question.

topics.title: Archive Dashboard
topics.description: View statistics and a summary of what is in your archive.

steps.text: Open the Dashboard from the right sidebar (the Statistics button). It shows a high-level view of your archive: record counts, import history, and data composition.
The dashboard shows counts for emails, messages, photos, contacts, and other imported data types — useful for confirming that imports completed successfully.
Ask the AI for richer summaries: "What is the earliest record in my archive?" or "How many emails do I have from 2020?"

topics.title: Identity Profile Wizard
topics.description: Use an AI-guided wizard to build a detailed identity profile of the archive subject.

steps.text: To seed the repository with information about the archive owner for the AI to base responses on, open the Profile Wizard from the bottom of the left sidebar. This wizard helps you create structured profile of the archive owner — their personality, values, life story, and more.
The wizard walks you through a series of questions to build a profile of the archive owner. Each section builds a different aspect of the identity profile.

Answer the questions in your own words. Be as detailed and factual as possible. Try not to filter your answers too much. Include any strong held feelings or beliefs you have about yourself or situations you have had
You can pause and resume the wizard at any point — progress is saved between sessions.
If you alread have a profile of yourself in a document, you can import it by pasting the text into the input field and clicking the Extract with AI button.
Once complete, the identity profile is stored in your archive and used to enrich AI responses — the AI will have a much deeper understanding of who the subject is.

topics.title: Local AI setup and health
topics.description: Understand Ollama readiness and required models.

steps.text: Local AI depends on the Ollama server plus two models: gemma4 and embeddinggemma. The gemma4 model is used for the main chat and the embeddinggemma model is used for the embedding search functionality and for image content classification.
On login screen, check the status of the local AI by selecting the "Local AI" tab to confirm the AI server status and model availability.
If a model is missing, use Download required models. Initial download can take several minutes.
Some AI features may be unavailable when Local AI is not ready.

topics.title: Setting up AI provider API keys
topics.description: Enter API keys for Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek to enable cloud AI providers.

steps.text: Open Configuration from the left sidebar, then switch to the API Keys tab.
Enter your Anthropic API key to enable Claude. Get a key at console.anthropic.com by creating an account and generating a key under API Keys.
Enter your Google Gemini API key to enable Gemini. Keys are available from Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com).
Enter your DeepSeek API key to enable DeepSeek — a cost-effective alternative that uses the same format as Claude but is typically much cheaper per token.
Keys are stored encrypted in your archive. They are never sent anywhere except directly to the respective AI provider when you make a request.
After saving, switch the AI provider in the voice settings panel and verify that a test question returns a response.

topics.title: Subject configuration
topics.description: Set the archive subject's name, pronouns, interests, and personality details.

steps.text: Open Configuration from the left sidebar, then switch to the Subject Configuration tab.
On the Subject Details and Interests subtab, enter the subject's full name, preferred pronouns, and date of birth. The AI uses these details in every response.
Add interests and topics the subject cares about. These are used by Today's Thing of Interest and to personalise AI responses.
Switch to the Writing Style subtab to describe how the subject typically writes and communicates — formal, casual, uses humour, etc. This shapes the AI's voice when speaking as the subject.
Switch to the Psychological Profile subtab for deeper personality context — traits, values, and how the subject handles emotions. This enriches AI responses in companion or interview modes.
Save after each subtab. Changes take effect immediately — the next AI response will use the updated configuration.

topics.title: Custom AI Voice Personas
topics.description: Create named AI personas with unique instructions and creativity settings.

steps.text: As well as the pre defined AI personae (voices) you can create your own custom AI voice personas. Open Configuration from the left sidebar, then switch to the Custom Voices tab.
Click New Voice to create a new persona.

Each custom voice has a name, description, and a detailed instruction block that tells the AI how to behave. Give the voice a name (shown in the provider dropdown, e.g. "Grumpy Professor") and a short description so you know what it is for.
Write the instruction in the Instructions box. Be specific: describe the persona's name, background, speech patterns, and any rules it should follow.
Set the Creativity slider — lower values give more factual, consistent responses; higher values are more expressive and varied.
Save the voice. It now appears in the provider dropdown in the voice settings panel — select it to switch the AI into that persona.

topics.title: Reference documents
topics.description: Upload documents that the AI can consult when answering questions.

steps.text: Reference documents are files you upload that the AI can read when answering questions. They are especially useful for providing context that is not in your archive — medical history, a biography, a family tree, or a personal statement.
Click the Ref Docs segment in the context bar below the chat input box or  "Import and Manage Reference Documents" in the DataImport tab to open the Reference Documents manager.
Click Upload Document to add a new file.
Supported formats include plain text, PDF, and Markdown. Add a title and description so the AI knows what the document contains.

Documents flagged Include in System Prompt are injected into every AI request — use this for a core context document. Documents flagged Available for Task are included only when the AI's tools call for them.

The Ref Docs count in the context bar updates to show how many documents are active. A warning icon means a document is flagged but unavailable or that no documents are available — check the manager for details.

topics.title: Import Facebook archive
topics.description: Step-by-step Facebook ZIP import flow.

steps.text: Request a Facebook data download in JSON format from Facebook. Select JSON format, then wait for the download email.
Unzip the downloaded file to a folder on your computer.
Open Import & Manage Data from the left sidebar.
Click Upload on the Facebook row and select the exported folder.

topics.title: Import Instagram archive
topics.description: Step-by-step Instagram ZIP import flow.

steps.text: Request a Instagram data download in JSON format from Facebook. Select JSON format, then wait for the download email.
Unzip the downloaded file to a folder on your computer.
Open Import & Manage Data from the left sidebar.
Click Upload on the Instagram row and select the exported folder.

topics.title: Import WhatsApp archive
topics.description: Step-by-step WhatsApp export and ZIP import flow.

steps.text: Export your WhatsApp chats from the app: in WhatsApp, open each chat → More options (three dots) → Export chat. Choose to include media. Do this for each conversation you want to import.
WhatsApp exports individual .zip files per chat. Collect them all into a single folder on your computer.
Open Import & Manage Data from the left sidebar.
Find the WhatsApp row in the import list, click Upload, and select the folder containing your exported WhatsApp ZIP files. The import processes each ZIP in turn.

topics.title: Import iMessage archive
topics.description: Import an iMessage export into your archive.

steps.text: Export your iMessage data from your Mac using a third-party export tool (such as iExporter or a direct copy of the chat.db file). The app expects the standard iMessage export format.
Open Import & Manage Data from the left sidebar.
Find the iMessage row in the import list and click Upload. Select the folder or ZIP containing your iMessage export. The import extracts messages and attachments.

topics.title: Import Mail via IMAP
topics.description: Connect your email account and import emails directly via IMAP.

steps.text: Email import uses the IMAP protocol to pull emails directly from your inbox and folders. No export file is needed — the app connects to email account and downloads messages.
Open Import & Manage Data from the left sidebar and switch to the Import tab.
Find the Email / IMAP row and click its import button.
Enter your Email address and, for the password, use an app password.(refer to your email provider for instructions on how to generate an app password).
Choose which mail folders to import and set a if you want to limit the import to new mail only. Click Start Import to begin.
Large mailboxes can take a long time to import. You can monitor progress in the Import & Manage Data panel. The app continues importing in the background.
After email import, the email embedding background job is run automatically so that similarity search works on your emails.

topics.title: Import photos from local disk
topics.description: Import photos and images stored on your computer into the archive.

steps.text: Open Import & Manage Data from the left sidebar and switch to the Import tab.
Find the "Link to Images on Disk" row. Click the link button to choose the root directory containing your photos.
Configure import options: set a maximum number of images to import and set whether the images get imported into the database or just linked to the archive as referenced media.
Click Execute. The app scans the folder recursively and imports supported image formats (JPEG, PNG, HEIC, etc.) including any EXIF metadata such as GPS coordinates and timestamps.

After a photo import, you can run the AI image classification background job from Import & Manage Data → Background Jobs to generate descriptive tags of the content for each photo — this greatly improves AI search and questions about images.

topics.title: Background jobs and maintenance
topics.description: Run scheduled and on-demand maintenance tasks: thumbnails, embeddings, and more.

steps.text: Open Import & Manage Data from the left sidebar.
Switch to the Maintenance tab to find one-off tasks such as rebuilding contact lookups, recalculating relationship strengths, and re-processing import data.
Switch to the Background Jobs tab to view and trigger scheduled jobs: thumbnail generation, message embeddings, email embeddings, and image AI classification.
Run the thumbnail job after a large photo import so images display quickly in the gallery. Run the embedding jobs after importing messages or emails to enable semantic similarity search.
Jobs run in the background — you can keep using the app while they execute. Check the job status panel to see progress and completion.

topics.title: Create and switch archives
topics.description: Manage archive profiles safely across users.

steps.text: Use login profile controls or admin archives to create and manage archive entries.
Switching archive changes the active SQLite database used for sign-in and chat.
Disabling an archive hides it from login selection without deleting data.

topics.title: Master key and sensitive data
topics.description: Understand the master key, what it unlocks, and how to use sensitive data records.

steps.text: The master key is a passphrase you set once that encrypts sensitive data records and unlocks advanced AI tool access. It is different from your login password and never leaves your device.
On sign-in, a prompt appears asking you to unlock with your master key. You can skip this, but sensitive data and some AI tools will be unavailable until you unlock.
Open Sensitive Data from the right sidebar to create and manage encrypted records — passwords, PINs, private notes, and any data you want kept locked.
Click Unlock to enter your master key and decrypt the sensitive data view. Once unlocked for this session, sensitive records are readable and the AI can use them if authorised.
Click + New Record to add a new sensitive data entry. Give it a name, category, and the secret value. All records are encrypted at rest with your master key.
The master key is set and changed via Configuration. If you forget your master key, encrypted records cannot be recovered — it is not stored anywhere.

topics.title: Sharing your archive with visitors
topics.description: Create visitor keys so others can access your archive with limited permissions.

steps.text: Visitor access lets you share your archive with another person — a family member, carer, or friend — who can browse and chat with the AI without seeing sensitive data or admin features.
Open Configuration and switch to the Manage Visitor Keys tab to create and manage visitor access.
Create a new visitor key and set a password hint. Share the archive URL and the visitor key password with the person you want to give access to. They log in using the share link.
Visitors see the same archive data but cannot access sensitive records, owner-only AI tools, or admin settings. They use the "Who's Asking?" switch set to visitor mode.
You can disable or delete a visitor key at any time to revoke access immediately.

topics.title: AI tools access control
topics.description: Configure which AI tools are available and what permissions they require.

steps.text: AI tools are the capabilities the AI uses to look up data in your archive — search messages, retrieve emails, find photos, and more. Each tool can be restricted by access tier.
Open Configuration and switch to the Tools Access tab.
Two tiers are available: Visitor (basic, lower-sensitivity tools available to all sessions) and Master (higher-sensitivity tools requiring archive owner access to use).
Select which tools are available for each tier. Sensitive tools — such as those that read private messages or decrypt sensitive data — should only be set to Master tier.
The Tools count in the context bar reflects how many tools are active for the current session tier.

topics.title: Local AI troubleshooting
topics.description: Recover quickly from common Local AI issues.

steps.text: If Local AI is unavailable, verify Ollama is running and both models are installed.
Re-open Local AI Setup and refresh statuses after model downloads complete.
If issues persist, use a cloud provider temporarily and retry Local AI later from Local AI Setup.

topics.title: Context window and long conversations
topics.description: Keep AI answers accurate across long chat sessions.

steps.text: Every AI provider has a context window — a limit on how much text can be in a single conversation. When a chat session grows very long, early messages may be dropped and the AI can lose context.
If you notice the AI forgetting earlier details, start a new chat session. Short, focused conversations generally produce better answers than very long, wide-ranging ones.
Local AI (Ollama/Gemma4) has a smaller default context window than cloud providers. If Local AI starts giving incoherent answers in long chats, switch to Claude or Gemini for that session.
You can clear the conversation history by clicking the voice image in the top right corner and selecting "Clear conversation history".

topics.title: AI usage tracking
topics.description: Monitor token usage and costs across AI providers.

steps.text: Every AI chat request uses tokens — a measure of text volume. Cloud providers (Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek) charge per token. Local AI (Ollama) is free but uses your CPU/GPU.
Click on the User button in the top right corner to download a PDF summary of your AI usage
If costs are a concern, switch to DeepSeek (a lower-cost Anthropic-compatible API) or use Local AI for everyday questions and reserve Claude or Gemini for complex tasks.

Very long system prompts (from reference documents included in the system prompt) increase token usage on every request. Only include documents in the system prompt if they are needed for most questions.
